title: fix(devx): resolve spec export conditions in the map's key order, and say which arm won
body:
Fixes #9408

`scripts/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts` resolved export conditions by walking its
**own** `['import','module','browser','default']` array, so a consumer-side
ranking overrode the precedence `@objectstack/spec` declares with its exports-map
**key order**. Both halves of the card are delivered: the direction is settled by
measurement, and the pick is now audible.

## The premise, re-measured on this base — it moved

The card names `./api` as declaring `['browser','import','require']`. On this
base (`@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, the installed pin) **it does not**:

```
./api  ["import","require"]     <- no browser arm at all
```

The defect class is real and **larger** than the card's instance — five entries
rank `browser` first, and they include the bare specifier:

```
.        ["browser","import","require"]
./data   ["browser","import","require"]
./system ["browser","import","require"]
./kernel ["browser","import","require"]
./cloud  ["browser","import","require"]
```

So the card's *mechanism* is confirmed and its *named subpath* is stale. Nothing
anywhere pinned the browser-carrying set, which is exactly how the move went
unnoticed — this PR pins it.

## What decides the direction

The card offered two fixes and declined to pick, warning that reordering the
array "would be wrong for any consumer that genuinely wants the Node arm". Three
measurements settle it.

**1. The hook disagrees with the resolver it exists to model.** Both sides in one
run, against the real installed package:

| specifier | this hook (before) | Vite, no override |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` | `dist/index.mjs` | `dist/browser/index.mjs` |
| `@objectstack/spec/data` | `dist/data/index.mjs` | `dist/browser/data/index.mjs` |
| `@objectstack/spec/system` | `dist/system/index.mjs` | `dist/browser/system/index.mjs` |
| `@objectstack/spec/kernel` | `dist/kernel/index.mjs` | `dist/browser/kernel/index.mjs` |
| `@objectstack/spec/cloud` | `dist/cloud/index.mjs` | `dist/browser/cloud/index.mjs` |
| `@objectstack/spec/api` | `dist/api/index.mjs` | `dist/api/index.mjs` |

An override build is supposed to differ from a normal build in **which spec** it
bundles, never in **which arm** of that spec it picks. That divergence is the bug.

**2. This repo has zero Node-arm consumers.** `resolveSpecDistInjection` has
exactly one production caller, `apps/console/vite.config.ts` — a browser build
that sets no `resolve.conditions`.

**3. Key order is correct for *both* kinds of consumer, and reordering is not.**
Under key-order resolution the consumer contributes the **set** ("these are the
conditions I satisfy") and the package contributes the **order**. A consumer that
wants the Node arm expresses that by dropping `browser` from its set — it no
longer has to fight a ranking baked into the resolver. Reordering the array only
swaps one consumer-side ranking for another, and would have broken exactly the
caller the card was worried about.

⇒ **direction (a): respect the export map's own key order.**

## The audible half

`SpecDistInjection` now carries the condition path that chose every entry, and
`formatConditionReport` renders the table the console config prints whenever the
override is live:

```
OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST: /…/@objectstack/spec
  19 exports entries aliased; condition arm chosen per entry:
    @objectstack/spec       browser > import > default  ->  dist/browser/index.mjs  [ranked above: import]
    @objectstack/spec/api   import > default            ->  dist/api/index.mjs
    …
```

Formatting lives with the resolver rather than in the config, for the reason
`specModuleTest` does (objectui#5388): one producer, so a second consumer cannot
drift into reporting an arm the resolver did not take.

## Tests

The existing Node cross-check **pinned the Node arm**, which is why this was
green: `import.meta.resolve` does not satisfy `browser`, so for a browser-first
entry it returns the Node arm by construction. It is not weakened — it is
**partitioned**, and a stronger oracle is added beside it:

- Node stays the oracle for the 14 entries it can express; the 5 it cannot are
  asserted to **diverge** from it, so the old behaviour cannot come back green.
- A **real Vite build** is the oracle for all 19, with an in-run control
  (`react`) — an oracle that resolved nothing would otherwise read as total
  agreement. (It did, first try, when the temp root sat outside the workspace.)
- Fixtures pin the algorithm in **both directions**: `browser` first takes
  `browser`; the same two conditions ranked the other way take `import`.
- `types` never being picked was incidental under the array walk and is
  load-bearing under a key-order walk — it sits first in every arm — so it is
  pinned on the fixtures too.

**Reverse verification** (direction predicted before running): restoring the
array walk → **4 red, and the `import`-first case stays GREEN**. That asymmetry
is the whole argument against direction (b); a one-direction fixture would have
ratified the bug. Mutation proven on disk by blob hash, restored byte-identical.

```
PRE   vitest scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts   exit 0   33 passed
POST  vitest scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts   exit 0   40 passed
POST  vitest --project unit scripts/__tests__/                      exit 0   4583 passed | 2 skipped (155 files)
POST  pnpm type-check:scripts                                       exit 0
POST  pnpm type-check:vitest-config                                 exit 0
POST  eslint (3 changed files, --no-inline-config)                  exit 0   5 pre-existing warnings, 0 added
POST  node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs                          exit 0
POST  node scripts/check-installed-spec-pin-claims.mjs              exit 0
POST  node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs                     exit 0   no changeset owed
POST  node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test       exit 0   NOT GOVERNED
ABLATION  array walk restored                                       exit 1   4 failed | 36 passed
```

No changeset: the gate confirms 0 of 3 changed files are published source of a
released package or a moved published contract.

## Not re-measured, deliberately

The card's cross-repo inference about objectstack#17535's +19.4% is flagged
unverified by the filer **and** by triage. This PR does not cite it, act on it,
or measure it. It is worth noting only that the sign of the question has changed:
under the override the console now resolves the browser arm it previously could
not reach.
